ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, assume $\odot O$ is the cross-section of a water pipe, with the width of the water surface $AB=48\,cm$, and the maximum depth of the water being $36\,cm$. What is the radius of $\odot O$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} As shown in the figure, draw $OD\perp AB$ at D, extend DO to intersect circle O at C, and connect AO,\\
According to the problem, $AB=48\text{cm}$, $CD=36\text{cm}$,\\
$\therefore$ by the Perpendicular Diameter Theorem, $AD=\frac{1}{2}AB=24$,\\
Let $OA=OC=x\text{cm}$, then $OD=CD-OD=(36-x)$,\\
$\because$ $AD^2+OD^2=AO^2$,\\
$\therefore$ $24^2+(36-x)^2=x^2$,\\
Solving for $x$, we get $x=26$,\\
$\therefore$ the radius of circle O is $\boxed{26\text{cm}}$.

method.method_draft: From the image, take AB as the horizontal water-surface chord and draw the vertical diameter through O, meeting AB at D, the lower circle point at C, and the upper circle point at E.
